entities.summary:
Chares of Lindos (b. 400 BCE, Lindus) was a musician or composer of the Classical era, an age of empires, philosophical inquiry, and foundational civilizations, active in Lindus. He was known for his contributions to the field of painting, where he was part of a prominent group of artists who collaborated with prominent sculptors.

Chares' most notable achievement was the creation of a series of paintings that adorned the walls of the Temple of Athena in Lindus. His work was highly regarded by the ancient Greeks, who saw him as a master of his craft.

The significance of Chares of Lindos lies in his role as a bridge between the artistic traditions of ancient Greece and the broader cultural landscape of the Mediterranean. His work reflects the cultural exchange and syncretism that characterized the Classical era, and his legacy can be seen in the many artistic and architectural achievements of the period.

This is evident in the many references to Chares in ancient sources, including the works of Aristotle and the Roman historian Plutarch. His art also influenced the development of Western art, with many artists, including Michelangelo and Raphael, drawing inspiration from his compositions.

Chares' impact on the development of Western art cannot be overstated. His innovative use of color and composition helped to establish the foundations of Western art, and his influence can still be seen in the works of many modern artists.

historicalSignificance.significanceNarrative: Chares of Lindos was a significant figure in the Classical era's artistic traditions, known for his innovative use of color and composition in his paintings. His work had a lasting impact on the development of Western art, influencing artists such as Michelangelo and Raphael.
